Museum
of CC0

A walkable web gallery that converts public-domain art into spatial browsing: enter a central hall, choose an artist doorway, approach a work, read its interpretation, and continue to the museum source.

Product shapeVirtual museum × spatial index × source gateway
Primary strengthDiscovery and context stay one interaction apart
Primary riskNo visible goal, memory or reason to return
Executive verdictWorth studying as a calm web-native exhibition shell; less convincing as a game until exploration gains memory, agency or curation.

01
Executive verdict

A spatial collection browser with the manners of a quiet museum.

The experience succeeds by reducing interface noise and letting architecture organize discovery. Its product ceiling depends on turning a pleasant first walk into a personally meaningful collection.

Observed

What works

Movement, labeled doorways, proximity descriptions and source links form an intelligible path from curiosity to context without quests, HUD clutter or account setup.

Observed

What is missing

No objective, completion state, collected history, bookmark, search trail, social room or persistent identity was visible. Exploration ends when curiosity does.

Product opportunity

Own the visit

Let visitors remember, group and share what held their attention. The highest-leverage evolution is curation, not points or combat.

Core promise: look longer
Positioning: not “a game about art,” but “a lightweight first-person museum that makes a public collection feel inhabitable.” This distinction should guide goals, accessibility and success metrics.
02
Why this experience

A clear visual hook and a credible technical story, not proven audience momentum.

Selection came from a team request. Public post engagement describes attention to the creator’s announcement, not museum visits or players.

Radar

Selection basis

The experience entered the teardown queue by team request after the public build and creator source were verified. That process establishes relevance and availability, not growth.

Creator post metrics

Public attention snapshot

The creator’s X post had 3,058 views, 30 likes, 2 shares and 4 comments when captured on September 16, 2026. These are post-level metrics; unique visitors, starts, completion and return are unknown.

Acquisition hypothesis

Immediately legible premise

A browser-based walk through familiar paintings is easy to demonstrate in a short clip. Famous public-domain works and spatial novelty explain interest more plausibly than game depth.

Counter-signal

No independent discovery graph

The saved snapshot contains no verified independent posts or momentum series. Creator reach and AI curiosity may dominate observed attention.

03
What the product is

A first-person, room-based interpretive layer over a finite art collection.

The player fantasy is not mastery. It is being alone in an approachable museum where every work can open into more context.

Observed

Genre and perspective

First-person browser exploration with free look, walking, proximity-based artwork interaction and doorway transitions between a central gallery and artist rooms.

Visible

Collection promise

The welcome panel states “A place to look a little longer,” names the collection size, says “Take your time,” and explicitly promises no time limit and no sound.

Likely audience

Who it serves

Casual art learners, educators, web-experience enthusiasts and visitors who prefer self-paced discovery over a database or long article. Motion-sensitive and keyboard-only users receive meaningful support.

04
Observed first visit

Instruction, orientation and deeper context arrive in the right order.

The session reached multiple artist areas, opened artwork interpretation, followed an external museum source and returned to the central gallery.

Read the welcomeLearn movement, look, interaction, pause and the calm visit promise.
Inspect settingsDiscover collection browsing, graphics, comfort and control options before entering.
Enter the hubArrive in a bright rotunda-like gallery with paintings, benches and labeled arches.
Choose an artistUse wall labels and sightlines to enter a dedicated artist room.
Read a workApproach or click a painting to open title, date, medium, interpretation and source.
Follow provenanceOpen the institution’s canonical artwork page in the browser.
Return and continueUse the gallery-return portal, then browse further artist doorways.
First payoff: the first contextual artwork panel proves that the 3D space is not decorative. It is a navigable index that connects visual encounter, interpretation and authoritative provenance.
05
Core loop

Orientation → attention → interpretation → provenance → onward curiosity.

The loop has no failure state and no imposed finish; the visitor self-selects depth.

1 · OrientRead doorway labels and room sightlines
2 · ChooseWalk toward an artist or visually salient work
3 · InspectFrame the artwork and open its description
4 · DeepenRead interpretation or visit the source museum
5 · ContinueEnter another room or return to the hub
06
Controls & interaction contract

Desktop-first inputs are explained before the visitor commits.

The product earns trust by exposing movement and comfort choices in a conventional document-like panel.

Visible

Movement

W/A/S/D walk through the gallery. Arrow keys or mouse look around. Exact acceleration, collision radius and diagonal normalization are not established.

Visible

Interaction

Click or Enter reads a painting or enters a doorway. Proximity can display descriptions when the comfort preference is enabled.

Visible

Pause and settings

Escape pauses and opens the settings surface. “Resume your visit” returns to the preserved world state; “Restore defaults” resets preferences.

Visible

Comfort

Motion behavior, text size, reading colors, field of view, walking speed and automatic approach descriptions are configurable.

Visible

Graphics

Graphics quality supports Automatic selection; frame-rate limit includes a 60 fps “smoothest” option. Changes apply immediately.

Unknown

Alternate devices

Touch, gamepad, screen-reader traversal, browser zoom behavior and mobile layout were not demonstrated. The reconstruction must not assume support without implementation.

07
Mechanics & rules

The rules are architectural rather than competitive.

Movement changes position; position changes available context; doorways change the collection slice.

08
Progression, economy & content

The collection is broad; progression is entirely mental.

Visitors gain context, not currency. The interface exposes breadth but does not remember personal progress.

Observed

Content structure

A central hall branches to rooms organized by artist. Visible labels include Rembrandt, Johannes Vermeer, Emanuel Leutze, Georges Seurat, Katsushika Hokusai, Gustave Caillebotte and Vincent van Gogh.

Visible

Artwork record

Records can include artist, title, approximate date, medium, interpretive copy, source institution and an external source link.

Observed

No economy

No purchase, ticket, virtual currency, unlock price, upgrade or gated exhibit was visible. External museum pages may have their own commerce, but that is not the museum’s in-world economy.

Unknown

No visit memory shown

The materials do not establish visited works, favorites, saved routes, completion percentage, resume position across sessions or account persistence.

Implementation choice

Gentle progression

Add a private visit journal: viewed, lingered, favorited and source-opened. Keep it opt-in and non-scoring so it reinforces looking rather than completion anxiety.

Content cost

Expansion model

Adding work requires licensed/public-domain imagery, normalized metadata, interpretation, provenance link, frame/aspect handling, room placement, lighting QA and accessibility text.

09
UX/UI reconstruction atlas

The interface alternates between two modes: inhabiting a room and reading a document.

The contrast is productive: spatial immersion handles discovery; paper-like panels handle precision, settings and provenance.

11
Visual system & presentation

Institutional restraint gives the paintings visual authority.

Warm floors, pale walls, deep green rooms and modest typography create coherence without competing with the collection.

#F4EFE5 · paper/walls
#173129 · ink/action
#4B5045 · world olive
#7D8575 · room sage
#B79659 · frame gold
#A34E37 · editorial accent

Typography

Display / titles: restrained transitional serif
UI / labels: neutral humanist sans
Artist wall labels: uppercase, wide tracking
Reading copy: 15–18 px equivalent, generous line-height
Keycaps: compact bordered monospace-like tokens
Numbers: ordinary proportional figures

Spatial language

Camera: eye-level first person
Light: broad skylight + focused wall spots
Geometry: arches, molding, columns, parquet/checker floors
Frames: dark wood and gold, aspect-aware
Navigation: visual sightlines before overlays
Decoration: sparse benches and classical vessels

UI geometry

Square corners, one-pixel rules, restrained borders and almost no ornamental shadow. Primary buttons use deep green fill; secondary actions use outlines or underlined text. Panels resemble catalog sheets rather than game menus.

Motion and sound

The experience explicitly states there is no sound. Transitions can be reduced, walking can stop without drift, and the renderer pauses when idle. No additional animation or VFX language was established.

Responsive/accessibility target: preserve the document UI as reflowable DOM; maintain 44 px controls; expose semantic headings and form labels; provide a 2D collection route when 3D input, motion or GPU support is unsuitable; do not make hover or proximity the only discovery mechanism.
12
Strengths & frictions

The experience respects attention; it does not yet cultivate continuity.

Priorities focus on orientation, provenance continuity and meaningful return rather than gamification.

P0

Preserve return context across external links

Opening an institution page can replace the museum and strand the visit. Use a new tab or explicit return affordance, persist room/camera state, and explain the handoff.

P0

Add orientation without a minimap takeover

The hub is legible, but deeper rooms can become symmetric. Offer a subtle breadcrumb—Gallery › Artist—and an always-available “Return to gallery.”

P1

Make visit memory visible

A private journal of viewed and saved works creates a reason to continue and return while respecting the non-competitive tone.

P1

Unify collection search and spatial location

Selecting a work should offer “View details” and “Visit in gallery.” The current catalog shortcut proves the data layer but its relationship to teleport/navigation was not demonstrated.

P2

Clarify doorway activation

Click/Enter handles both paintings and doors. Add a consistent focus outline or small verb label so visitors know which nearby object will activate.

Strong

Complete onboarding

The first panel explains every essential desktop action and offers both spatial and catalog entry.

Strong

Comfort-aware design

Motion, FOV, walking speed, text size, reading colors and approach behavior are first-class preferences.

Strong

Provenance forward

Institution links keep the experience connected to authoritative records instead of presenting interpretation as an isolated truth.

13
Social, viral & return loops

The current hook is shareable spectacle; the product itself is solitary.

Public feedback points toward curation, the most natural bridge from isolated visit to social object.

Observed

Current return drivers

Collection breadth, famous works and unexplored artist rooms can extend a first session. No rotating exhibit, recommendation, saved state or notification was visible.

Public source

Curated rooms

Public feedback proposed user-curated rooms and shareable exhibitions; the creator endorsed the idea. Implementation is not confirmed.

Best social artifact

A room with a thesis

A visitor selects 5–12 CC0 works, writes a short wall text, chooses a layout and shares a walkable URL. The artifact carries taste and narrative, not merely a screenshot.

Return loop

Visit journal

Resume unfinished rooms, revisit favorites, compare a prior path and receive one optional themed route. Avoid streaks and scarcity that contradict “Take your time.”

Unknown

Current social infrastructure

No account, multiplayer presence, comments, UGC publishing, room code, leaderboard or collaborative visit was shown.

14
Growth interpretation

Famous art, browser immediacy and an AI-build story explain attention better than game mechanics.

Each factor has a different acquisition role and a different durability risk.

Idea / visual hook

Walking among canonical paintings communicates instantly in screenshots and clips. Counter-signal: once novelty fades, the current loop offers limited personal ownership.

Known cultural works

Van Gogh, Monet, Rembrandt, Vermeer and other recognizable names lower comprehension cost. This is cultural familiarity, not licensed-IP fandom.

Platform distribution

A direct web link removes installation friction and is easy to share. Rendering performance, input expectations and browser compatibility become conversion risks.

Creator audience

The measured attention belongs to a creator announcement on X. There is no basis to separate existing audience reach from product-driven spread.

AI narrative

The creator describes the gallery as generated with GPT‑6 Astra. That story can attract technical attention, but it does not prove art-historical quality or durable visitor value.

Public feedback

The curation/share idea suggests users immediately saw a platform beyond the demo. It remains a suggestion, not evidence of shipped social behavior or retention.

Performance contract

Load the hub and onboarding before noncritical rooms. Stream artist-room textures on approach. Cap texture memory, preserve artwork sharpness over decorative detail, pause render on still/hidden state, and never reveal an untextured work as complete.

Content integrity contract

Every displayed work must resolve to one canonical record. Validate public-domain/CC0 status and source URL before publish. Keep interpretive copy distinct from institution-provided text and store alt text independently from visual description.

Vertical slices: 1) welcome + one hub wall, 2) movement and comfort, 3) one artwork focus card, 4) one artist room and return portal, 5) collection browser, 6) external provenance handoff, 7) full content import and visual QA, 8) optional visit journal.
18
Acceptance specification

Test calm, continuity and content correctness as rigorously as rendering.

A faithful reconstruction must preserve hierarchy, copy, movement contract and provenance behavior.

First entry

Given a new visit, when the build becomes ready, then the welcome panel shows collection promise, all core controls, primary entry, collection access and comfort access before world input is active.

Keyboard onboarding

Given welcome focus, when the visitor uses keyboard only, then every action is reachable in logical order and Enter activates the focused choice.

World entry

Given Enter the museum, when critical assets are ready, then the visitor spawns grounded in the central gallery with stable orientation and readable artwork sightlines.

Movement

Given exploring state, when move/look input occurs, then the camera responds without drift, does not cross walls, and respects configured speed, motion and field of view.

Artwork focus

Given an actionable painting, when Click or Enter is used, then the matching artist, title, date, medium, description and source render while the artwork remains visible.

Panel close

Given artwork information is open, when Close or Escape is used, then focus returns to the world without changing room or camera.

Doorway transition

Given an artist doorway, when activated, then movement pauses, a neutral loading state appears if needed, and the visitor enters the correct room at a safe spawn.

Return path

Given an artist room, when Return to the gallery is activated, then the central gallery restores without an accidental re-entry loop.

External provenance

Given a valid source link, when it opens, then the destination is clearly external and room, camera and focused artwork context can be restored.

Pause/settings

Given active exploration, when Escape is pressed, then walking and rendering stop, settings receive focus, and Resume restores the same visit state.

Immediate preferences

Given a graphics or comfort change, when a value is selected, then the supported effect applies immediately and persists through pause/resume.

Collection consistency

Given an artwork selected in Collection, when its record appears, then title, artist, image and provenance match the in-world placement.

Loading failure

Given a room or artwork asset cannot load, when the timeout resolves, then a readable retry/return state replaces blank geometry and the current visit is preserved.

Visual regression

Given supported desktop and narrow widths, when welcome, settings, hub, room, artwork info and return portal are captured, then panels do not overflow, paintings retain aspect ratio and all primary copy remains readable.

19
Experiments, confidence & unknowns

Test personal meaning before adding conventional game progression.

The opportunity is to increase depth and return without damaging the quiet-visit promise.

High confidence

Reconstructable

Welcome copy and controls, central/artist-room composition, doorway hierarchy, artwork cards, source handoff, settings categories, collection browser, visible art count and no-sound/no-time-limit promise.

Unknown

Needs validation

Complete artist/work inventory, mobile and gamepad support, all control settings, error states, persistence, room streaming, loading duration, texture sourcing, metadata pipeline, analytics, privacy, hosting, backend and current implementation of curation.

Confidence boundary: this specification can reproduce the observed desktop visit and its explicit UI states. It cannot claim exact hidden geometry, source code, asset pipeline, unvisited rooms or long-term behavior.

The Museum of CC0 already knows how to make art approachable. Its next product question is how to make a visit belong to the visitor.

Evidence basis

Behavior and chronology come from the observed visit; layouts, copy and settings come from captured interface states; creator, technology and post metrics come from the saved Radar record and linked primary sources. Architecture and experiments are labeled recommendations.

No hidden implementation, unverified player metric, complete collection claim beyond visible copy, or unseen feature behavior is asserted.
